items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: And then in my thirties I tried to play a little classical music with Joanne Geller.

ctx.x: It was the John Jaski school of accordion. I played the accordion when I started, when I was about eleven and a half or something. That’s how I started. I took a couple of years of accordion lessons. That was basically it. And then a few — along the way I did, you © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-

know, a lesson here or there, I took a couple of lessons with Jim Straney, but I actually didn’t have a piano then. So that was kind of weird. And then in my thirties I tried to play a little classical music with Joanne Geller. But basically I took — the kid who lived upstairs from me, his family was right from Italy, and you know, the neighborhoods in the fifties how they were — he played the accordion and his cousin would come over, a guy who would play the mandolin and they’d be on the porch in the summer and…
